sources.title: Catálogo de jogos PlayStation Plus para outubro: Mafia: The Old Country, Horizon Forbidden West, Mycopunk e muito mais
sources.text: Dino Crisis 2 e RollerCoaster Tycoon 3 Complete Edition chegam no PlayStation Plus Deluxe. Neste mês, mergulhe no submundo do crime da Sicília do início do século XX em Mafia: The Old Country, enfrente uma fronteira mortal repleta de máquinas impressionantes em Horizon Forbidden West ou encare hordas de inimigos fúngicos com um arsenal extravagante de armas futuristas no jogo de ação cooperativa frenética Mycopunk, todos chegam no catálogo de jogos do PlayStation Plus já em outubro. Enquanto isso, o PlayStation Plus Premium recebe Dino Crisis 2 e RollerCoaster Tycoon 3. A lista completa de títulos estará disponível para jogar em 20 de outubro, salvo indicação em contrário. E, com a chegada da temporada de Halloween, os membros da PlayStation Plus podem aproveitar uma seleção de ofertas exclusivas como parte das nossas comemorações do Horrorfest. Confira os detalhes completos abaixo desta publicação. Descubra as origens do crime organizado nesta conturbada história de máfia ambientada no submundo brutal da Sicília do início do século XX. Lute para sobreviver como Enzo Favara e prove seu valor para a família nesta envolvente ação em terceira pessoa, que se passa em um momento histórico perigoso e implacável. Esta fantástica história ganha ainda mais vida com os visuais impressionantes, a narrativa cinematográfica e o realismo autêntico que consagrou a fama da aclamada série Mafia. A história de Enzo se passa em uma época em que a destreza com uma lâmina de estilete era letal, a espingarda lupara de cano cerrado era a arma de fogo preferida, vinganças sangrentas se prolongaram por décadas e os mafiosos patrulhavam seus territórios a pé, a cavalo ou ao volante dos primeiros automóveis. Acompanhe Aloy ao enfrentar o Oeste Proibido em uma fronteira majestosa, mas perigosa, que esconde novas e misteriosas ameaças. Explore terras distantes, enfrente máquinas maiores e mais imponentes e conheça novas tribos extraordinárias neste retorno ao futuro distante e pós-apocalíptico de Horizon. Reencontre velhos amigos, firme alianças com novas facções em conflito e desvende o legado de um passado ancestral — tudo isso enquanto tenta manter-se um passo à frente de um novo inimigo aparentemente invencível. Fatie alienígenas fúngicos neste jogo de tiro com saque baseado em missões e com altíssimo nível de personalização. Centenas de melhorias feitas à mão, modo cooperativo para 4 jogadores e um pequeno homem-barata. Como não amar? Um esquadrão de robôs rejeitados é contratado pela corporação SAXON e recebe uma última chance de conquistar a glória e alguns lucros (e evitar o ferro-velho). É a Equipe de Risco de Novo Atlas, um esquadrão de exterminadores em frangalhos enviado para descobrir os mistérios por trás de uma catástrofe fúngica que afeta todo o planeta. Embarque numa série de missões perigosas no planeta para afastar a ameaça micológica. Será um simples desastre natural como alegam? E será que a SAXON não fez direito a sua declaração de imposto de renda? Ou foi culpa sua? Mycopunk chega ao Catálogo de Jogos PlayStation dia 20 de outubro. Após um confronto com Huggy Wuggy e libertar Poppy, você deve descer mais fundo na fábrica de brinquedos da Playtime Co. Quebra-cabeças desafiadores e brinquedos horripilantes aguardam. Use ganchos, balance-se e abra caminho com força até a segurança. Tente escapar, e não deixe a mamãe encontrar você. Continue explorando as profundezas da Playtime Co. em busca de respostas. Sua jornada para descobrir o que aconteceu dentro da fábrica está apenas começando… Poppy Playtime: Chapter 2 estará disponível em 27 de outubro. Embarque em The Midnight Walk, uma aventura de fantasia sombria e reverente moldada em argila, criada pelas mentes por trás de Lost in Random, Fe e Ghost Giant. Torne-se o The Burnt One, faça amizade com uma criatura-lanterna perdida chamada Potboy e use a chama dele para iluminar seu caminho por um mundo de contrastes, repleto de maravilhas e horrores. Sobreviva e supere com astúcia os muitos monstros ávidos por devorar a chama do seu amiguinho enquanto vivencia cinco contos de fogo e escuridão, com um elenco incrível de personagens peculiares. Encante-se com cada detalhe perturbador de uma paisagem meticulosamente criada à mão com argila real e animada no estilo stop-motion. Totalmente jogável tanto no PS5 quanto em RV – com o PS VR2. The Midnight Walk estará disponível hoje, 14 de outubro. Tales of Arise – Beyond the Dawn Edition | PS5, PS4 Por 300 anos, Rena dominou Dahna, saqueando os recursos de seu planeta e privando as pessoas de sua dignidade e liberdade. Nossa história começa com duas pessoas nascidas em mundos diferentes, cada uma procurando mudar seu destino e criar um novo futuro. Com um elenco diversificado de personagens, um sistema de combate intuitivo e gratificante e uma história cativante ambientada em um exuberante mundo pelo qual vale a pena lutar, Tales of Arise oferece uma experiência de JRPG excelente. Tales of Arise – Beyond the Dawn Edition estará disponível em 27 de outubro. Monster Energy Supercross 25 – The Official Video Game | PS5 Vivencie a emoção de correr em pistas recém-projetadas que replicam eventos do mundo real e dispute com a mais recente lista de pilotos profissionais: abra o caminho em uma carreira renovada com competições intensas, rivalidades e escolhas estratégicas. Graças ao Unreal Engine 5, aproveite um gameplay renovado com física realista e evolução dinâmica da pista, tornando cada volta única e desafiadora. Domine o fluxo com tutoriais abertos, uma wiki abrangente e assistência de pilotagem da Neural Technology. Monster Energy Supercross 25 – The Official Video estará disponível em 27 de outubro. Um ano se passou desde os eventos de “Operação: Resgate do Dr. Kirk”. A pesquisa e desenvolvimento liderados pelo governo continuam para o projeto Third Energy do Dr. Kirk, conhecido por seu potencial em produzir fontes de energia limpa e sua capacidade de destruição em massa. Um dia, uma catástrofe temporal oco

stories.title: Take-Two CEO’s Response To Second GTA 6 Delay: “Please Tell Me You’re Kidding”
stories.summary: Rockstar's GTA 6 is finally coming out on November 19, but the game was originally set to release in 2025. When the development team informed head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, that a delay to May 2026 was necessary, she made a call to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick to let him know. Months later, she had to make that call again, informing Zelnick that a second delay to November 2026 was required...

sources.name: GameSpot
sources.title: Take-Two CEO’s Response To Second GTA 6 Delay: “Please Tell Me You’re Kidding”

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: "Please tell me you're kidding": GTA 6's two delays flabbergasted Take-Two CEO
sources.text: "A lot of people would say, ‘You’d just better figure out how to ship it.’ The two GTA 6 delays might have been frustrating for you, but they were definitely worse for Strauss Zelnick, CEO of the game's publisher, Take-Two Interactive, who reportedly asked the unfortunate Rockstar dev who told him about them if they were "kidding." Speaking to Bloomberg , Rockstar's head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, said she had to call up Zelnick twice - once when GTA 6 was delayed out of Fall 2025 to a May 2026 date , and then again to say that it needed a second delay, this time from May to November . The second time, Zelnick struggled to take the news. "I think he said, 'You're kidding. Please tell me you're kidding'," Kolbe says of her second call with Zelnick. Thankfully, the Take-Two CEO was pretty understanding in the end: "Once we talked through why, he got it. And I think we are really lucky that he is as reasonable as he is, because a lot of people would say 'you just better figure out how to ship it'. And we have been really, really lucky that we have not found ourselves in that place, because that happens to a lot of teams, and we've all played those games. It's not great." We've definitely seen the results of games that are pushed too early - Cyberpunk 2077 springs immediately to mind, in spite of its redemption arc, but many others have launched too soon and never gathered the momentum they needed to thrive. Granted, in this case, Zelnick is in the enviable position of having the biggest launch of the decade waiting in the wings, meaning the extra year of investment in GTA 6 will probably amount to little more than a rounding error in its eventual bottom line. GTA 6 took 13 years, but GTA 7 won't – Rockstar says "the tools and the team we've built during this project will allow us to do things more quickly" in the future. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more I'm GamesRadar's Managing Editor for news, shaping the news strategy across the team. I started my journalistic career while getting my degree in English Literature at the University of Warwick, where I also worked as Games Editor on the student newspaper, The Boar. Since then, I've run the news sections at PCGamesN and Kotaku UK, and also regularly contributed to PC Gamer. As you might be able to tell, PC is my platform of choice, so you can regularly find me playing League of Legends or Steam's latest indie hit. sources.title: When Rockstar Needed To Delay GTA 6 Again, Take-Two’s CEO Replied: ‘Please Tell Me You’re Kidding’
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 GTA 6 Rockstar Games Strauss Zelnick In May 2025, Rockstar announced it was delaying Grand Theft Auto 6 until May 2026. Then, a few months later, it announced it was delaying GTA 6 again to November 2026 . For many fans, these back-to-back delays were excruciating and disappointing. And for Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, it apparently seemed like a prank. On October 14, Bloomberg published a lengthy report about Rockstar Games and its work on GTA 6 , its upcoming open-world crime simulator that is set to be the biggest game release of the decade when it arrives on November 19. However, remember that when the game was first revealed in December 2023, Rockstar promised a launch window of 2025. According to Rockstar’s leaders, they believed that was possible, though some devs below them weren’t convinced. But as they got closer, Rockstar North’s head of development and coâstudio head Rob Nelson realized they needed more time. âYou feel a huge pressure and obligation to deliver the highest-quality game in the most aggressive time scale that you can,â Nelson told Bloomberg . âAnd then you keep evaluating it as you go. And then you have to decide when you get within striking distance of that if it is actually achievable.â So the devs told Rockstar head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe to phone up Take-Two boss Zelnick to ask for more time, which he granted . Then a few months later in 2025, Kolbe had to ring him up again to ask for another delay, this time pushing GTA 6 back until November 2026. âI think he said, âYouâre kidding,'” recalled Kolbe. “Please tell me youâre kidding,ââ âBut once we talked through why, he got it. And I think we are really lucky that he is as reasonable as he is, because a lot of people would say, âYouâd just better figure out how to ship it.â And we have been really, really lucky that we have not found ourselves in that place, because that happens to a lot of teams, and weâve all played those games. Itâs not great.â Zelnick explained that it’s usually a “wise investment in time” and resources to give devs more time and delay a game’s launch in order for it to âreach the level of perfection it has the ability to reach.â Still, I get the feeling that was not a fun call for him or Kolbe.Â Donât miss the latest reviews, news and tips. sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Ex-ZA/UM developers reveal Red Rooster, an "incendiary RPG" that is very intentionally not trying to be a "Disco Elysium successor" or "Disco-like"
sources.text: Back in 2024, we heard about the formation of Summer Eternal : a new studio composed of Disco Elysium writer and world-builder, Argo Tuulik, and other veteran ZA/UM staff such as Dora Klindžić, Anastasia Ivanova, and Michael Oswell. Aleksandar Gavrilović, secretary of the Croatian Game Development Alliance, and Lenval Brown, Disco Elysium's narrator, are also part of the crew. Since then, we've heard nothing from the new collective, but earlier this month, the studio got in contact with me to gauge interest in the Summer Eternal Anthology, a 500-page physical book that's part-treatise on the cultural and labour impact of the video game industry, and part-development journal for its newly-announced "incendiary RPG", Red Rooster. In Red Rooster, you play as Redrick Roost, a white-collar inmate thrust into the role of an arson investigator who partners up with an opiate-dependent mathematician. Together, they investigate a string of arson that all seems to connect to Redrick's brother who is none other than - you guessed it! - the city's fire chief. Per Summer Eternal, the game is set in a "fractalised border archipelago" of the tri-partie city of Arta-Tantor. It's all very political alternate history stuff, with a "strong science-fiction undercurrent". As Red Rooster's tagline puts it, "Fight fires to get to the truth of your world. Start fires to get to the truth about yourself." Summer Eternal is calling Red Rooster an "incendiary, physics-driven RPG combining the best of cerebral, worldbuilding-rich RPGs with the genetics of physics-driven immersive sims". Very ambitious, then. The studio also notes the game is "fully physics-driven" and full of objects you can move, manipulate, and burn - the team wants you to "exert your physical existence" upon the world. "RPG worlds are often static, frozen maps," it says. "We're aiming to build the urban archipelago of Arta-Tantor into a reactive playground of physical interactivity and evolving human stories through scripted and emergent events." Red Rooster is being built in Unreal Engine to make use of advanced physics engine features, and the studio adds it's "breaking away from isometric constraints to drop you into a three-dimensional world with dynamic camera movement. " Elsewhere in the release, it name-drops Expedition 33's Sandfall Interactive, noting the collective is aiming for a "double-A production budget" similar to the "compact team" that worked on 2025's breakout RPG. Summer Eternal says the game is "nearing the end of pre-production" and that an internal playable tech demo already exists. The book shows a little of this, and while I appreciate the team is trying to put distance between itself and Disco Elysium, you can't help notice the similarities in some aspects. Below, you can see a quick pic I snapped of the eponymous Red Rooster - he bears more than a passing resemblance to Harrier 'Harry' Du Bois, right? Elsewhere in the game, there's 'The Coop', which is reminiscent of Disco Elysium's psychological manifestations in the 'Thought Cabinet'. Here, Red's internal mental space is populated by roosters; versions of himself that represent different motivations, urges, and personalities. Summer Eternal references games like Exanima, Half-Life: Alyx , Vampire: The Masquerade: Bloodlines, Dark Messiah of Might and Magic, Arcanum: Of Steamworks and Magick Obscura, Planescape: Torment , and Larian's Divinity engine games as inspiration. Influences outside of games include Chris Carter's Millenium, Fringe, Netflix's Dark, Better Call Saul, Fargo, and the works of Ted Chiang and John Steinbeck. A lot of this information comes from the book that's been used to announce the game, and the Summer Eternal Anthology is a very interesting read. It includes interviews about the state of games and tech with economists Yanis Varoufakis and Richard Wolff, a chat with science fiction visionary (and one of my favourite authors) Ted Chiang, conversations with Bioware veterans Mark Darrah and David Gaider, as well as stories from worker-run organizations such as the UVW-CWA, Aftermath, and Peregrine Coast Press (who are wonderfully described as "paper perverts"). If you'd like a copy yourself, you can purchase one here - it's €69 for the Standard edition, and €99 for the Deluxe Firestarter bundle that comes with a vinyl and additional merch. If you buy a copy of the book, you will also be entitled to a membership in the Summer Eternal Players Non-Profit organisation, which owns five percent of Summer Eternal; giving you a vote on matters regarding studio governance, and having a say in how five percent of profits generated by Red Rooster are used in the future. You can join that initiative here . Summer Eternal, of course, isn't the only studio to have been born from the fracturing of ZA/UM's original team. There's also Longdue , an independent studio comprising former Disco Elysium staff, and Dark Math Games , a team that refers to itself as a "breakaway group from the original development team of Disco Elysium". ZA/UM also carried on as a development unit, and the studio launched Zero Parades: For Dead Spies back in June, before laying off a large chunk of its remaining staff . Prior to the multi-part split of Disco Elysium talent, game director Robert Kurvitz and art director Aleksander Rostov alleged that ZA/UM management had gained ownership of the studio and its intellectual property fraudulently, with the two claiming that they were "summarily fired and cut off from our life's work" after they began asking for financial records from ZA/UM's new owners. Counter-allegations of mismanagement and misconduct followed, and it only got messier from there . Back in 2024, in a feature I worked on at VG247 , game director Argo Tuulick told the site "he'd rather under-promise and over-deliver" when it comes to this game. This book, though, seems to have moved on from that maxim, and may well be one of the most ambitious project statements I've ever seen.

sources.name: Gematsu
sources.title: Summer Eternal announces ‘incendiary, physics-driven RPG’ Red Rooster for PS5, Xbox Series, Switch 2, and PC
sources.text: Summer Eternal , one of the multiple studios founded by former Disco Elysium developers, has announced Red Rooster , an “incendiary, physics-driven RPG.” It will launch first on PC , with plans for PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series , and Switch 2 versions to follow. A release date was not announced. The reveal is accompanied by a 500-page physical book titled “ Anthology Volume One ,” showcasing the game’s concept art, design, and world building. The book will be delivered to “thousands of fans” within 48 hours from today, and the Deluxe Edition ships with a limited edition 10-inch vinyl featuring four tracks from the game’s soundtrack. Here is an overview of the game, via its official website : Red Rooster is an incendiary, physics-driven RPG combining the best of cerebral, worldbuilding-rich RPGs with the genetics of physics-driven immersive sims. Play as Redrick Roost, a white-collar inmate thrust into the role of an arson investigator and partnered up with an opiate-dependent mathematician to investigate a mysterious string of arson that all seems to connect to his brother, the city’s fire-chief. Explore the fractalized “border archipelago” of the tri-partite city of Arta-Tantor in a political alternate-history setting with a strong science fiction undercurrent. Fight Fires to Get to the Truth About the World Events of Red Rooster take place in an our-world-adjacent magical realism setting. It’s an all-new fictional world inspired by a fusion of the 1980s sun-drenched Yugoslavian riviera and the Eastern Block, with influences ranging from the Ottoman culture to Scandinavian social-democracies and the colonial Dutch Empire. This is not the “end of history,” but rather the “beginning of the future” in the tripartite city of Arta-Tantor. In the last days of the longest summer on record, the city is hosting the 13th triennial Continental Summer Games while the region is ravaged by an unprecedented heatwave, sporadic power-outs and a troubling amount of domestic and wildfires. Set Fires to Get to the Truth About Yourself Step into the ankle-monitor-clad boots of Redrick “Rooster” Roost, a white-collar inmate serving a life sentence in a minimum security prison for gross criminal negligence over a highly publicized auto-meditation device fiasco. A week before your parole hearing, you’re approached by a high-ranking official from a low-profile government agency with a proposal to infiltrate the local fire station run by your brother and identify the serial arsonist suspected to be operating amongst their ranks. In exchange for your help, you’re promised a blanket pardon for your crimes and a guaranteed return to the society you haven’t been a part of for more than a decade. You don’t have face the flames alone. Join forces with an opiate-dependent mathematician, Dr Astrid Albers, and a nunchaku-wielding truth-activist, the district bus driver Rico. Three’s a company after all. And you’re gonna need all the company you can get, as the fires you face become increasingly harder to explain and the destructive urges harder to ignore. Navigate the flames, the intrigues and the politics of Arta-Tantor as you prepare for the parole hearing, respond to fire incidents, follow the arsonist’s trail and try to blend in with the firefighters of Terminal 9. Or give in to the seductive whispers of Redrick’s dark alter egos in the bizarre ‘chicken coop’ he has constructed inside his head as you wrangle Redrick’s mind in the signature psychological RPG fashion. Who are you really when the lights go out?

sources.title: Gran Turismo 7’s Spec IV (Part 1) launches today and a first look at DualSense wireless controller – Gran Turismo Limited Edition
sources.text: The latest update includes the legendary Sugo Circuit, six new vehicles, and more ways to experience your driving passion. Hey everyone, we’re excited to share news on Gran Turismo with you today. For starters, we have full details on today’s Part 1 of the Gran Turismo 7 Spec IV update. Plus, we celebrate 30 years of Gran Turismo with the first look at the Gran Turismo Limited Edition DualSense wireless controller! Read on for full details. Today, all players will receive Part 1 of the Gran Turismo 7 Spec IV update. Whether you’re chasing lap times, discovering automotive history, capturing the perfect photo, building your dream collection, or simply looking for something new to drive, Spec IV adds new ways to explore the world of cars with six new vehicles, the Sportsland Sugo circuit, new events, Scapes locations, gameplay features, and more. Also arriving in this update are new Car Viewer features, Experience mode, 6 new World Circuit events, and much more! All of this will be available for free beginning today at 11:00 pm PDT / October 15 at 7:00 am BST / 3:00 pm JST*. Xiaomi Vision Gran Turismo is an electric hypercar sculpted by the wind. Its teardrop-shaped cockpit is embedded within a body sculpted with cutouts and air ducts, forming aerodynamic channels throughout the vehicle. The signature halo-shaped taillight serves as both a visual icon and a massive air outlet. Together with innovations like the Active Wake Control System and Accretion Rims, the car achieves a drag coefficient of 0.29, downforce of -1.2, and an aerodynamic efficiency rating of 4.1 through iterative simulated testing, reaching new heights in balancing low drag and high downforce for electric hypercars. “Electric hypercars must answer a fundamental question,” said Tianyuan Li, Design Head of Xiaomi Auto. “Do we pursue extreme low drag for straight-line speed, or maximum downforce to conquer corners? The optimal solution lies in finding the perfect balance between the two.” This approach impressed Gran Turismo Series Producer Kazunori Yamauchi. “When I saw that Xiaomi had resolved the contradiction between low drag and high downforce, I was truly amazed.” Try this in GT7: Take it to the Spa-Francorchamps circuit in the Vision Gran Turismo Trophy event and see how its futuristic design translates to one of racing’s most historic circuits. Ferrari, the brand of the Prancing Horse, based in Maranello, Italy, has raised cars to the realm of art, pouring technology and passion built in racing into its production cars. And one car that carries on the lineage of their midship sports cars, is the F355 Berlinetta of 1994. The body by Pininfarina is a masterpiece combining beautiful curves and functional beauty. The square lines of the 348 has greatly evolved, balancing aerodynamic performance and sensual beauty at a high level. Just looking at the car makes your heart race – a look of a true Ferrari Try this in GT7: Head to the Sportsland Sugo circuit and let the Ferrari’s balance and responsiveness come alive through the circuit’s flowing corners and elevation changes. The Mugen Motul Civic, which won the overall class victory at the 1987 All-Japan Touring Car Championship, was a Group A race car developed from the twin-cam ‘Si’ model that joined the 3rd generation Civic line-up in 1984. The Civic Si Group A version featured in Gran Turismo is based on this Mugen Motul Civic. stories.title: Grand Theft Auto IV – The Legacy Review
stories.summary: Obsessively detailed and impressively timeless, GTA IV is the prototype for modern Grand Theft Auto.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Grand Theft Auto IV – The Legacy Review
sources.text: I’m taking a look back at each of the core Grand Theft Auto games and replaying them in the lead-up to the arrival of Grand Theft Auto 6. What we’ll be putting together won’t be traditional re-reviews, and they won’t come with any new IGN score, but they will re-examine what made each GTA remarkable upon the time of its release. By the end of the project, using GTA’s previously six-star wanted level, you should be able to get an idea of where each of these games roughly rank in my long-term love for this series. Today it’s time to revisit Liberty City in Grand Theft Auto IV. Grand Theft Auto IV is smaller than GTA: San Andreas. Significantly so, if you exclude water, as its land area is reportedly around only one-quarter the size of San Andreas’s physical real estate. GTA IV also has markedly reduced vehicle variety, with much fewer of them overall and zero car customisation. It has no asset management, less mission variety, no RPG-inspired skill system, a pretty paltry list of cheats, and the only thing you can alter about lead character Niko Bellic is his outfit. In fact, if you weren’t around for the arrival of GTA IV, I think it’s fair enough that you may actually find yourself a little confused about its place in the series pantheon. That is, how could this apparently smaller game with overtly fewer features than its predecessor have instantly become not only the highest-rated GTA in the history of the series, but one of the highest rated games of all time, full stop? Well, the devil is in the details. Countless, unprecedented, incredible details. For all his faults as an Eastern European war veteran with a shady past and a short temper, who may or may not have spent 106 minutes trying to kill Owen Wilson back in 2001, Niko Bellic has actually carved out a place as one of the most likeable and accessible characters in the franchise. Lured by his cousin Roman’s lies of wealth and opportunity, it’s easy to both sympathise with Niko’s disappointment at his first encounter with the American Dream, and share in his distaste for the various bastards of Liberty City who seek to exploit him. Released in 2008, GTA IV was the first game in the series to be set in the present day since GTA III. In 2026, it’s an interesting snapshot of the world just prior to the smartphone takeover – back when the internet was still a destination you took time out to visit on a computer, social media was still a novelty rather than the worst thing to happen to humanity since disco music, and your radio would always let you know you were about to receive a mobile phone call. However, despite the 18 year gulf between its setting and today, GTA IV doesn’t feel remotely as retro as something like GTA: Vice City did in 2002 – even though there were only 16 years between its setting and the time of its release. The aesthetic distinctions between the ’80s and 2000s are, of course, profound. What are the visual differences between the 2000s and now, other than the fact The Rock used to have hair? It’s not a long list. Monoculture is dead, fashion is looping, and – as remarkably detailed as GTA IV is – I don’t think there’s anything Rockstar could have done to dodge this phenomenon, Dwayne Johnson’s shaven skull notwithstanding. However, even though the feeling I glean from GTA IV being a depiction of a specific moment in time may not be as strong as that elicited by either GTA: Vice City or GTA: San Andreas, there is no denying what a victory it is in terms of its capacity to represent a true sense of place . GTA IV’s Liberty City wasn’t just one of the most convincing virtual cities of its generation; I honestly don’t think it’s an overstatement to say its commitment to tiny details still stands up to scrutiny today. Revisiting GTA IV’s Liberty City in 2026 – a game that my Xbox 360 play data indicated to me I haven’t touched in around 14 years – I’m immediately reminded of how fastidiously crafted every corner of this world is. Yes, it’s a smaller environment than that of San Andreas, but it’s one that is so much more crowded, dense, and dripping with depth. It’s more immediate, more authentic, and more intimate than anything that came before it – and it’s still a more credible and convincing city than those in most of the open-world action games I’ve played since. Strolling though Star Junction – Liberty City’s glitzy Times Square proxy – I find myself in tourist mode. I’m too engaged by the fact there’s something to see, read, or admire everywhere I point the camera to be distracted by the temptation of causing anti-social chaos. Hoofing it through Hove Beach – inspired by Brooklyn’s Brighton Beach – and I’m once again impressed at how much mileage Rockstar extracts from the seemingly mundane. Garbage strewn on the sidewalks. Individualised storefronts that are faithful to the demographics of the area and are never repeated elsewhere around the city. Places with stories you’ll never get to the bottom of. Like, who is Mikey Pissroll, and how much better at pool is he than Anal Alan? The architecture, the lighting, the lived-in grime; Liberty City here feels more than real. It feels aged . Rockstar didn’t just build streets; it built them, and then assaulted that asphalt with decades of simulated wear. As a result, those streets are a patchwork of potholes, road plates, and sporadic strips of more recently re-surfaced segments. The custom signwork, the bespoke graffiti – the fact that no piece of the city looks like any other. A multitude of elements combine to create what was an unprecedented sense of immersion at the time, and absolutely still holds up today. Sure, there’s an unavoidable murkiness to playing GTA IV on original hardware like the Xbox 360, where you’re obviously beholden to the resolution limitations of its age. It results in a soft and rather muted image, and one that’s admittedly exacerbated by the overly cool and slightly washed out colour palette Rockstar opted for. However, it’s still a stunnin

sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 rumored to be launching on PC sooner than anyone expected, but I wouldn't get my hopes up too high
sources.text: If the rumored release window is accurate, it means the new GTA will hit PC just a few months after consoles—something almost unheard of from Rockstar. A GamesBeat report claims that Grand Theft Auto 6 —which still hasn't been announced for PC—will launch for PC sometime within the first three months of 2027. If correct, that means the game will drop, at most, just four months after its initial release on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles. GamesBeat cites "four industry sources familiar with the studio's plans" in its report, all of whom requested anonymity. Rockstar has not yet commented on the claim. It's a surprising claim. Earlier this year, we predicted that GTA 6 won't likely appear on PC before November 2027 , mainly because that's just how Rockstar rolls. We always have to wait. Compared to that, a four month break between the console and PC releases, and possibly less, seems downright snappy, especially given how the gaps between GTA games themselves have grown over the decades. Not only would a Q1 release of GTA 6 on PC be an unusually brief break, it also puts the game in the midst of the post-holiday hangover, when we're all doing our best to nurse our bruised and battered bank balances back to health. And that, I think, would feel especially egregious in the immediate aftermath of this year's holiday season, which for gamers will be driven by the release of GTA 6 on consoles. Rockstar loves the double dip , but punching the button again so soon after the console release would surely be viewed dimly by a not-insignificant number of people who would prefer the flexibility and power of the PC, but really don't want to wait for it. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. Of course, if Rockstar or Take-Two confirms the GTA 6 PC release date really is that close—Take-Two's next quarterly financial report takes place on November 9, which might be a time for such a thing—some no doubt would wait for it, cannibalizing launch sales to some extent. There's no shortage of people on social media saying they will indeed wait to buy GTA 6 if the PC version is indeed coming that quickly. That feeling may be even more widespread than it appears, given how much GTA 6 costs: At $100 for the premium edition and all the exclusive content it contains, you can understand why people might be more reticent about buying it multiple times than they were for earlier games in the series. Anything's possible, of course, and I would never presume to have a better understanding of these things than Strauss Zelnick and the rest of the GTA brain trust. But I also wouldn't bet on it—and for now I'm definitely taking all of this with a grain of salt. I've also reached out to Rockstar to ask about it, and will update if anyone answers. GTA 6 guide : Everything we know GTA 6 cars : The garage lineup GTA 6 characters : Your anti-hero cast GTA 6 map : Confirmed Vice City locales GTA 6 PC release : When's it going to happen? Andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from new game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill. sources.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Preorders Are $10 Off at Amazon and Walmart
sources.text: In case you missed the memo, physical copies of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time are currently discounted at the likes of Amazon and Walmart. There's a $10 discount at both major retailers in the US, bringing the game down to $59.88 instead of $69.99. Preorders for Ocarina of Time have been live for a little over a month, and there's a jolly good reason everyone is so excited about it. It looks stunning, and we're now closer than ever to getting our hands on it. But what's the deal with the immediate $10 discount at retailers like Amazon and Walmart? Well, it's actually fairly simple. As is Nintendo's custom for this console generation , the MSRP for the game is $59.99 for digital copies and $69.99 for physical copies. But to encourage fans to buy physical games via their online storefronts, Amazon and Walmart have been fairly consistent at knocking prices down to match or even beat the digital price. That's consistent for other Switch 2 exclusives such as Star Fox , Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave , and Switch Sports Resort , to name a few. But it's important to note that once the game is released, the price goes back up. So this is purely an incentive to preorder games. So that's the deal! Plus, there's an even better reason to own The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as a physical copy as well. Nintendo also announced that the first printing of physical copies of the game would include "textured foil cover art" ... but only available while supplies last! Plus, for what it's worth, for physical copies, the complete full game comes on the cartridge . No game key card. Therefore, if you're down for a shiny textured foil cover for the game, which is limited edition, then your best bet is to preorder with Amazon or Walmart, and lock down your copy ASAP. Plus, as a reminder, Amazon's preorder price guarantee means you don't have to pay for the game until it ships, and if there are any further price drops, you'll pay the lowest price possible (even if it goes back up in price before release day on November 5, 2026). The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches for Switch 2, November 5, 2026. It'll have more than redone load screens when it arrives, with players also still coming to grips with the wild changes Nintendo made to the game's visuals . For more of what we saw during The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct, you can read about the Link & Epona Lego set and the special edition console . For everything else revealed, click here . For more on Ocarina of Time, check out IGN's preview of the remake - alongside this brand new feature where we discuss 29 new changes that are present in the new Switch 2 version of the game, including redesigned puzzles, updated miniboss fights, deeper dialogue, and more. If you've been after the Z elda 40th Anniversary Switch 2 as well, it might be worth checking out Amazon, as the console has been going in and out of stock all week. Add it to your wishlist, and keep an eye on it throughout the day, and you should be able to secure it before October 29. Robert Anderson is a Senior Commerce Editor for IGN. Based in London, UK, he is a qualified journalist with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (First Class Degree) and over seven years of professional writing and editing experience. You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV. sources.title: Ocarina of Time Remake Will Support All Existing Zelda Amiibo With In-Game Item Bonuses
sources.text: Nintendo just dropped a new overview trailer for the Ocarina of Time remake, offering a fresh look at revamped environments, characters, and combat. We had the chance to play some of the game ourselves , and were surprised by just how many changes Nintendo is making to the iconic N64 release. While Nintendo previously announced two new amiibo figures tied to the remake - Young Link and Young Zelda - the new overview trailer also confirms support for all existing Zelda amiibo. It doesn’t go into too much detail about what that support will involve, but the trailer shows Link receiving a number of helpful items, including healing hearts, Green Potions, and a Deku Stick. Your quest through the vast kingdom of Hyrule begins when The Legend of #Zelda: #OcarinaOfTime comes exclusively to Nintendo Switch 2 on Nov 5. Pre-order now: https://t.co/FNWvsJDFej https://t.co/peIRfkTMJh It appears players can tap existing Zelda amiibo for helpful consumables and items, but not necessarily any exclusive cosmetics or weapons. This is similar to how non-Zelda amiibo worked in Tears of the Kingdom , which allowed for daily “bonus” scans of general Amiibo once per day. The previously announced Ocarina of Time amiibo, which are up for preorder with varying levels of stock across retailers, will net players wearable masks for Zelda and Link. Nintendo first launched the amiibo product line with the Wii U. Each amiibo comes with a small figure as well as a card that you can scan from Nintendo consoles, netting players various unlocks and bonuses across games. Every mainline Zelda release has been accompanied by new amiibo. Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom Amiibo offered in-game weapons and gear in addition to daily rewards. Amiibo frequently sell out in the lead-up to big game releases, and Zelda is about as big as it gets. While the Switch 2 generation of amiibo continues to be in stock at most retailers, some of the older releases have pretty much disappeared from the internet. For those who are desperate to get their hands on an older release, GameStop offers tons of pre-owned amiibo with a solid ‘Pre-Owned’ guarantee for peace of mind. You’ll also find third-party resellers at Target, Best Buy, and eBay, though it’s always worth comparing prices to a figure’s MSRP at release. sources.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has new boss rematches with built-in speedrun tracking
sources.text: You better believe I'm showing King Dodongo what for By all appearances, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2 seems to be a one-to-one remake of the original N64 classic, faithful down to the details of every dungeon puzzle. But there are at least a few all-new features in here beyond the quality of life tweaks, including a special hall where you can marvel at defeated enemies and battle bosses all over again. "Somewhere in this world lies the Hall of Fallen Foes," the game's new overview trailer explains. "Statues of defeated monsters reside here. You can learn about them or engage in rematches with powerful foes." You can walk up to statues and hit a button to take a close-up look, with a bit of flavor text describing the monster and a list of main locations where it appears. With bosses, you can hit a "rematch" button to take on the creature again. A timer will tick up during the battle, and your time will be recorded when you complete the rematch, so you'll have a convenient way to track speedruns against individual bosses. The hall itself seems to take inspiration from the Nintendo Gallery that appeared in The Wind Waker, where you could take photos of characters and enemies from throughout the game and have them turned into a series of collectable figurines. As a Zelda lore-obsessed 13-year-old at the time of Wind Waker's original release, I loved the opportunity to catalog the game's inhabitants, and I'm glad the Ocarina of Time remake will offer something similar. After two hours of hands-on time with the Ocarina of Time remake , Andy says it feels like a homecoming and a true Zelda celebration. Personally, I remain a bit skeptical that a straight remake can live up to the stature of what the original game meant back in 1998, but I'll happily accept a few surprises to make this familiar journey a little fresher in 2026. These are the best Zelda games of all time. Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week Dustin Bailey joined the GamesRadar team as a Staff Writer in May 2022, and is currently based in Missouri. He's been covering games (with occasional dalliances in the worlds of anime and pro wrestling) since 2015, first as a freelancer, then as a news writer at PCGamesN for nearly five years. His love for games was sparked somewhere between Metal Gear Solid 2 and Knights of the Old Republic, and these days you can usually find him splitting his entertainment time between retro gaming, the latest big action-adventure title, or a long haul in American Truck Simulator. sources.text: Remake Switch 2 The Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time The first hands-on previews for the Switch 2’s remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time just dropped alongside a fresh overview trailer . While much of what people have played is a retread of the early sections of the game first revealed during last month’s Nintendo Direct, the hours-long sessions also allowed players to go off the beaten path and dig into some of the nuances of what is changing in this new version of the Nintendo 64 classic. Here are five additional details we just learned about the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Â remake . In the original game, you were limited to holding just 99 rupees at the start. Per IGN , you now start off with a wallet that can hold twice that. This used to be an upgrade players unlocked for turning in 10 Gold Skulltula Tokens to the cursed family in Kakariko Village. It’s unclear what the new prize will be instead. IGN also notes that the Forest Temple has received a significant overhaul in some areas. This includes everything from changes to how some of the puzzles work to decorative renovations like color-coded motifs for each different section of the dungeon to make it more obvious which section you’re in. One mini-boss fight replaces a bottomless pit with a pool of acid. Nintendo also stuck an elevator shaft in one area to minimize some of the backtracking. I can only guess how extensive the revisions might be to more complicated dungeons like the Water Temple. The N64 game only had four bottles. Getting the final one required Link to hunt down 10 Big Poes across Hyrule Field. A Nintendo rep confirmed to IGN that a fifth space in the inventory screen is indeed for an additional bottle. It remains to be seen if players unlock it over the normal course of the game or there’s now a new puzzle or mini-challenge for them to complete.Â It’s called The Hall of Fallen Foes and it shows Link all of the enemies he’s defeated in the game. As teased in a new overview trailer , it sounds like the big owl Kaepora Gaebora will carry the Hero of Time back and forth from the new location. Players will be able to do rematches against bosses like Dodongo and Shadow Link. It’s unclear if there are any extra prizes to unlock but each fight will have a time trial counter to show you how fast you’ve completed it. Ex- Giant Bomb writer Jeff Gerstmann uploaded his B-roll footage from the event which showed, among other things, just how many times Navi will stop Link to tell him about the world or just gab via word bubbles during the normal course of exploration. The first time you run into a Peahat Larva in Hyrule Field, for instance, Navi freezes the game and goes through a miniâlore dump about the monster. Other previewers have confirmed that some NPCs in the game have a bit more flavor to their dialogue and additional lines that provide more world building than in the original game. I’m excited to trick my six-year-old into practicing his reading this way. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake has a new item that summons Business Scrubs to you! stories.title: "I was forced to ship the game" - Glen Schofield blames Krafton management for The Callisto Protocol's problems
stories.summary: Glen Schofield, the game-maker best known for co-creating Dead Space, has blamed Korean company Krafton - the owner of PUBG - for the shortcomings of his horror game successor The Callisto Protocol , which it published. Read more

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: "I was forced to ship the game" - Glen Schofield blames Krafton management for The Callisto Protocol's problems
sources.text: "A lot of them were caused by Korean management." Glen Schofield, the game-maker best known for co-creating Dead Space, has blamed Korean company Krafton - the owner of PUBG - for the shortcomings of his horror game successor The Callisto Protocol , which it published. In an interview with GamesIndustry.biz , Schofield expressed frustrated bewilderment at Krafton's handling of his Striking Distance company, which it had invested in, during the Covid pandemic. Krafton allegedly promised Striking Distance three extra months of development time and then rescinded it. "I was forced to ship the game," Schofield said. "I'm mad at myself, there's no doubt. I was so stunned by that decision, because we had fucking Covid. A million people died in America. I lost one of my best friends. "Every single month, four to six people in my company were getting sick. There were times [when] our small team in Spain was shut down; it goes through a small place like that and you lose your rendering team for a while. "The main thing you're concerned about, not that you aren't normally, is the health of your team. Making a game just became secondary because this is about life. This is about humanity." Schofield has discussed the decision to deny the three extra months of development time before . Had it not, then The Callisto Protocol would have been released in March 2023, rather than December 2022. This sudden rug-pull had also come after years of the studio adapting to working during a pandemic already, which Schofield said had been very hard to do. "When you have a studio of a hundred people, you can touch a hundred people a day. When they're at home, you have to do individual calls, or I could get everybody together on Zoom," said Schofield. "But we did it. We did all these things because we were searching for the best way to do it. There were so many meetings. "We had to learn on the job and just change everything," he added. "We got it done and everything. We saw the problems that we had. A lot of them were caused by Korean management." Before it was embroiled in a legal battle with Subnautica 2 creators , Krafton was mostly known as the PUBG company. Having found so much success with the battle royale shooter and its off-shoots, the publisher was ready to invest in the triple-A space - but it seemingly wasn't ready for that new role. Schofield said Krafton lacked the necessary experience to release a single-player physical game, forcing Striking Distance to build an internal team to do that. Krafton also allegedly mandated a release of The Callisto Protocol on PlayStation 4 alongside PS5, which would cost "another $20 million", Schofield said, and require sending out 200 dev kits to developers during a global chip shortage. None of that helped The Callisto Protocol's fortunes, and Krafton wasn't happy with its financial performance as a result. "[Krafton] thought Callisto was a complete failure," Schofield revealed. "What they didn't know while all they were doing was complaining, we were doing patches. I waited until I finished all the DLC and put out 86 patches. That was a lot of fucking work. Every day you're going in, you're making changes. Some are little, others are massive. That was all to get it back to where it needed to be." The Callisto Protocol received a mixed reception at launch, owing to technical and performance issues but also to core design elements relating to combat. In the Eurogamer review of The Callisto Protocol , Vikki Blake praised the game's production values but lamented its lack of depth and tension compared to Dead Space.

sources.title: GTA 6 Was Originally Meant to Release Much Sooner Than We Realized
sources.text: Rockstar Games has revealed that it originally intended to develop GTA 6 alongside Red Dead Redemption 2, meaning it probably would've come out much sooner than we ever realized. As told in a new article from Bloomberg , Rockstar Games initially planned to develop Red Dead 2 and GTA 6 at the same time, but that quickly became infeasible. Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson recognized that the ambition behind Red Dead Redemption 2 meant they would need to treat it as an all-hands-on-deck situation, which also meant putting GTA 6 on the back burner. However, GTA 6 would benefit from this, as Nelson noted to Bloomberg that everything they built for Red Dead would "pay off" in GTA 6. That appears to be true, as GTA 6 uses a lot of ideas and systems from Red Dead Redemption 2, including its NPC interaction system. It seems unlikely that GTA 6 would be what it is today if it had stayed the course and been developed in tandem with the western sequel. Unfortunately for fans, it means the game took much longer to make. Had it been developed simultaneously, it seems likely that Rockstar would've been able to release GTA 6 in the early 2020s. Of course, the first release window that Rockstar ever actually publicly provided for GTA 6 was 2025. The game was delayed a couple of times, much to the bewilderment of Strauss Zelnick, the CEO of Rockstar's parent company, Take-Two Interactive. Rockstar's head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe noted that she had to call Zelnick just months after announcing the game's first delay to inform him that they would need more time. “I think he said, ‘You’re kidding. Please tell me you’re kidding,’” recalled Kolbe to Bloomberg. “But once we talked through why, he got it. And I think we are really lucky that he is as reasonable as he is, because a lot of people would say, ‘You’d just better figure out how to ship it.’ And we have been really, really lucky that we have not found ourselves in that place, because that happens to a lot of teams, and we’ve all played those games. It’s not great.” Bloomberg's report dispels rumors that GTA 6 has been in active development since shortly after GTA 5 was released in 2013, but that doesn't mean Rockstar only began working on it after Red Dead 2's launch. Various teams and leadership within Rockstar have been researching and planning GTA 6 since as early as 2014. Rockstar has spoken at length in recent interviews about taking staff to Florida to research and dream up ideas for GTA 6 during the mid to late 2010s. Bloomberg noted that the team didn't have a "skeleton" for GTA 6's story until the end of 2019, a year after Red Dead 2's release. Even then, it took a while before the team was able to fully wrap its head around what the game would be. Rockstar has vowed to not take nearly as long on its next game , thanks to the fact it seems to have fewer obstacles going forward. Rockstar doubled in size during GTA 6's development, encountered multiple leaks, had a loss in productivity during the pandemic, and much more. The studio also made major changes to how it operates and expects that will set it up for success moving forward. What is Rockstar's next game? We don't know. Some may expect Red Dead 3, but other fans are hoping that Rockstar will break the cycle of alternating between Red Dead and GTA in favor of something new or reviving a different IP. Whatever the case is, don't expect it to take another eight years. Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

stories.title: Estúdio brasileiro comemora lançamento de Deep Dish Dungeon no Game Pass: “É um privilégio para nós”
stories.summary: The post Estúdio brasileiro comemora lançamento de Deep Dish Dungeon no Game Pass: “É um privilégio para nós” appeared first on Xbox Wire em Português .

sources.name: Xbox Wire BR
sources.title: Estúdio brasileiro comemora lançamento de Deep Dish Dungeon no Game Pass: “É um privilégio para nós”
sources.text: Saulo Camarotti estava explorando uma masmorra no famoso jogo de sobrevivência Valheim quando teve uma ideia: “Essa dungeon sozinha poderia ser um jogo muito legal”, ele relembra em uma conversa com o XBOX Wire. Dois anos depois, esse jogo se tornou real e está sendo lançado como Deep Dish Dungeons no XBOX Series X|S hoje, 13 de outubro, e disponível desde o primeiro dia para assinantes de XBOX Game Pass Ultimate. Em antecipação à chegada de mais um jogo brasileiro ao Game Pass, conversamos com Saulo para explorarmos juntos essa masmorra de Deep Dish Dungeon , talvez até encontrar alguns segredos…. Gênero : Dungeon Crawler/Survivor/Metroidvania Desenvolvedora : Behold Studios Publicadora : Raw Fury Plataformas : Steam, XBOX Series X|S, XBOX no PC e Portátil Modos : solo ou multiplayer até 3 jogadores online Funcionalidades : XBOX Play Anywhere e Cross-Play (Steam e consoles XBOX) Idioma : português Brasileiro nas legendas e interface Em Deep Dish Dungeon controlamos um explorador em busca de tesouros em uma masmorra, sozinho ou na companhia de amigos. E é isso. Uma premissa simples e sem muitos rodeios, já que a ideia, segundo Saulo, nunca foi guiar o jogador para onde ele deve ir. “Eu queria criar uma experiência sobre explorar uma masmorra como um aventureiro e não como um guerreiro”, explica o desenvolvedor. “Não é sobre matar, morrer e ganhar nível. Esse é um jogo em que você tenta entender esse lugar antigo em ruinas e tenta sobreviver”. Com esse foco em exploração, Saulo diz que Deep Dish Dungeon tem uma média de 15 horas de duração até ser finalizado. Enquanto o jogador descobre mais sobre o tesouro que está buscando, e o próprio lugar em si por meio de narrativas espalhadas pelo cenário, surge uma das mecânicas de jogos mais importantes: cozinhar. Já dizia o ditado: saco vazio não para em pé… nem explora, por isso que é fundamental preparar comidas que dão vantagens ao jogador – daí o “Dish” (prato de comida em tradução livre) no nome. “Você come antes de se aventurar. Não é depois, para se curar”, explica Saulo. “E cada categoria de ingrediente no jogo dá uma vantagem diferente, como mais vida ou vigor”. Foi nesse aspecto da culinária que a Behold colocou um tempero de brasilidade ao jogo, com ingredientes como semente de guaraná e mandioca (ou macaxeira ou aipim dependendo da região do país) ou quitutes como coxinha , pastel e bolo de fubá que podem ser preparados. Dá até água na boca. Alguns exemplos de efeito de ingredientes: A própria presença desses ingredientes típicos do Brasil também dá dicas da localização dessa masmorra, apesar do jogo nunca revelar de fato onde é. “O jogo acontece num lugar fictício, mas para nós, internamente, está mais ou menos ali na Amazônia”, revela Saulo. A partir desse conceito, o time se baseou nas criações de elementos de arte e arquitetura que compõe o lugar. Outra caraterística importante em Deep Dish Dungeons é que masmorra que o jogador explora é fixa e não criada proceduralmente. Saulo diz que isso foi uma decisão proposital. Para que cada lugar, obstáculo e segredo foi pensado para dar um senso de progressão que é mais próximo dos jogos no estilo “Metroidvania” do que os de Survival. “A masmorra é toda interconectada que nem um Metroidvania, e à medida que você encontra ferramentas e ganha habilidades, você consegue abrir novas salas e explorar mais a fundo”, explica o desenvolvedor. Essas ferramentas podem ser achadas pelo cenário ou criadas com recurso coletados durante a exploração. Ao obter um martelo , por exemplo, é possível quebrar portas de ferro que antes bloqueavam uma nova área. Já criar um gancho abre possibilidades de agora ir a lugares elevados que podem ter passagens secretas ou dar acesso a novos ambientes. Deep Dish Dungeon é o primeiro título da Behold Studios a chegar no XBOX Game Pass. No Brasil, o estúdio ganhou notoriedade na década passada ao lançar sucessos indies como Knights of Pen & Papper e Chroma Squad , mas Saulo diz que o novo jogo representa uma nova fase para eles, de projetos com produções rápidas e de escopo simples, mas eficaz. O novo game foi desenvolvido em apenas dois anos e por uma equipe de duas pessoas: Saulo na direção, programação e Game Design, e Carolina Baumgarten na arte. Por isso, a visibilidade dada pelo Game Pass foi o estímulo muito bem-vindo para o estúdio nesse momento, como a refeição que dá benefícios antes da exploração da masmorra, ou nessa, caso, do lançamento do jogo. Saulo também explica que estar no Game Pass impulsiona um dos aspectos mais importantes de Deep Dish Dungeon : o multiplayer. Apesar de poder ser jogado sozinho, o jogo foi pensado, desde o início, para ser uma experiência compartilhada junto com outras pessoas em cooperação. “Criar uma comunidade multiplayer nesse tipo de jogo é essencial”, diz Saulo. ““O nosso jogo é multiplayer e cross-play. Então, se você está jogando no Game Pass, pode chamar um amigo que tá no Steam”. Então, reúna seus amigos exploradores, estejam eles no console ou no PC, prepare os suplementos, cozinhe um bolo de fubá e saia para descobrir os segredos e tesouros de Deep Dish Dungeon , que já está disponível exclusivamente nos consoles para XBOX Series X|S, XBOX no PC e no XBOX Game Pass Ultimate.
